findings.explanation: Splunk_TA_nix has no linux:cgroup sourcetype or cgroup memory script; its documented sourcetypes are cpu, vmstat, df, ps, top, linux_secure, etc. dataSources and detailedImplementation repeat the claim, so readers will look for an input that does not exist.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ([Splunkbase 833](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/833)) supplies linux:cgroup scripted reads and syslog ingestion for memory controller files
findings.suggested_fix: Describe linux:cgroup as a custom scripted input (optionally packaged in a local app beside Splunk_TA_nix) that reads memory.events/memory.current/memory.max per docker-<id>.scope, and list its output fields.

findings.explanation: description contradicts spl and dataSources: linux:cgroup lives in index=os, and the alert conditions are an oom_kill counter increase (critical), memory_current_pct > 95 (warning) or slope > 8 MiB/min with pressure > 80% (warning), not 'memory_max_bytes > 0'.
findings.quote: using `index=docker` sourcetype `linux:cgroup`, grouped by `host`, `container_name`, `merge_key`. Outputs `max_observed_rss_bytes`, `memory_current_pct`, `slope_bytes_per_min` each `the scheduled window`; alert when `memory_max_bytes` > 0
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite: 'Per host and container, raises critical when the cgroup memory.events oom_kill counter increases in the last hour (corroborated by kernel oom-kill printk lines and docker action=oom events), and warning when memory use exceeds 95% of memory.max or grows faster than 8 MiB/min above 80%; suggests a limit 30% above the observed peak.'

findings.explanation: There is no product called 'Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Containers', and the hostmetrics receiver scrapes host-level cpu/memory/disk/filesystem/network/process metrics, not per-container cgroup memory or oom_kill counters.
findings.quote: Alternative collection: Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Containers hostmetricsreceiver cgroup memory scrape exported through HEC
findings.suggested_fix: Name the Splunk Distribution of the OpenTelemetry Collector with the docker_stats receiver (container memory usage/limit) and state that it does not expose oom_kill counters.

findings.explanation: memory.events.local appears to have been introduced earlier (around Linux 5.2); the kernel floor is repeated in detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: memory.events.local for nested attribution requires Linux 5.7 or newer
findings.suggested_fix: Check the kernel cgroup-v2 documentation / git history for when memory.events.local was added and state that version.

findings.explanation: Template scenarios; none describe real OOM false positives.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `host`, `container_name`, `merge_key` — Health checks in `docker` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: deliberate stress/chaos tests; batch jobs sized to hit the limit and retry; JVM/.NET heaps sized near the limit producing sustained >95% without kills; page cache counted in memory.current inflating pressure; counter resets when a container is recreated (new cgroup) and duplicate kills when v1 and v2 hierarchies are both scraped.

findings.explanation: The closing checklist is generator residue addressed to the author, not implementation guidance.
findings.quote: confirm no forbidden narrative phrases from the gold contract errata

findings.explanation: join max=0 means unlimited matches, so it allows rather than avoids fan-out when container_owner.csv has duplicate host/container rows.
findings.quote: The closing join type=left max=0 with inputlookup container_owner.csv mirrors gold governance patterns and avoids multi-match explosions.
findings.suggested_fix: Say max=0 keeps every matching row and require container_owner.csv to be unique per host+container_name.

findings.explanation: The SPL uses no data model and Performance.Memory describes host memory, not per-container cgroup kills; equipmentModels lists kubernetes_k8s although the text says Kubernetes is out of scope. The Splunk Connect for Docker reference URL points to the Splunkbase home page instead of app 4496.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark Performance as optional host-level context only, set equipmentModels to Docker Engine / Linux cgroup models, and link https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4496.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: All three multisearch arms contain stats (and the third streamstats/sort); multisearch accepts only purely streaming subsearches, so the search fails to run. Aggregate after the fan-in or use append.

The syslog arm filters with '| search (match(_raw, ...) OR ...)'; the search command does not evaluate eval functions, so it looks for literal terms and the printk arm returns nothing. Use '| where match(_raw, ...)' or plain search terms.

oom_kill_count_15m is computed over a one-hour window (earliest=-1h@h) and resets are not handled; a recreated container gets a new cgroup with a lower counter, which max(0, last-first) hides only partially. Rename the field and handle counter resets.
toString() (camelCase) is used throughout; the Search Reference documents lowercase tostring() and states eval expressions are case-sensitive. Confirm it parses.
Host-level Performance memory percentage > 90 does not detect container OOM kills and would not reproduce any critical row of the primary search.

summary: The cgroup-first OOM narrative, docker events action=oom correlation and troubleshooting cases are strong, but the app/dataSources credit Splunk_TA_nix with a linux:cgroup input it does not ship, the description misstates index and thresholds, and the SPL cannot run (stats/streamstats inside multisearch, eval functions inside search).
